question: A meeting will be held only if all three members A, B and C are present. The probability that member A does not turn up is 0.10, member B does not turn up is 0.20 and member C does not turn up is 0.05. The probability of the meeting being cancelled is :
explanation:
**Step 1:** Calculate the independent probabilities that each individual member will be present at the meeting using the complement rule: $P(A) = 1 - 0.10 = 0.90$, $P(B) = 1 - 0.20 = 0.80$, and $P(C) = 1 - 0.05 = 0.95$.
**Step 2:** Find the joint probability that all three members turn up simultaneously so that the meeting can be held: $P(\text{Held}) = P(A) \cdot P(B) \cdot P(C) = 0.90 \times 0.80 \times 0.95 = 0.684$.
**Step 3:** Use the complement rule to calculate the probability that the meeting is cancelled: $P(\text{Cancelled}) = 1 - P(\text{Held}) = 1 - 0.684 = 0.316$.
